tagline: Across a long, narrow green where the county once held court.
intro: Out of the Rockville side, Route 74, the Tolland Stage Road, runs east into Tolland and cuts straight across the town green, a long and narrow strip set north to south with Route 195 along its western edge. East of the center the road follows the Tolland County Turnpike, laid out in 1809, which took tolls until its company was dissolved in 1834.

Two town halls face each other at the south end of the green, and the Congregational church and the old county buildings stand near where Route 74 crosses it. Most of the houses date from the 18th and 19th centuries. Tolland was the county seat until the courts mostly went to Rockville in 1890.

moments.title: Old Tolland County Courthouse
moments.text: The Federal courthouse of 1822 housed the town library from 1899 to 1985, and in 1930 the whole building changed hands for one dollar.

moments.title: Old Tolland County Jail
moments.text: Across the street the stone jail of 1856 held prisoners until 1968, and some former inmates have come back to tell visitors about their days in the Hollyhock Hotel.

moments.title: Hicks-Stearns Family Museum
moments.text: Built in 1788 as a tavern, the house got its tower and porch from Ratcliffe Hicks, whose will paid to start the school of agriculture that opened at UConn in 1941.
